# goldbot — status and next steps

Canonical design: `docs/DESIGN.md` (exported from the original Claude design doc; edit it here from now on).
Standing instructions for Claude sessions: `CLAUDE.md`. Owner's VPS guide: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.

## Where things are (as of 2026-10-05)
- The approval window no longer trusts the wall clock alone (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 60; needs trading-safety review).
  `Proposal.expired` was `time.time() > created + window_s`, so a backward clock step stretched the owner's 90 s
  window and a pending file stamped in the future (a restored backup, a bad write) stayed approvable. Now
  `window_over` (goldbot/telegram/approvals.py) uses the heartbeat rule of BACKLOG 58: a `created` more than
  `CLOCK_AHEAD_TOLERANCE_S` (5 s) ahead, or not a finite number, counts as expired. The bus, the outbox, the dashboard
  list and the digest all use it. The digest counts such a pending proposal as EXPIRED_UNAPPROVED. The engine's
  `ApprovalCenter` also keeps a monotonic deadline per proposal it raised, set at `propose` to now + `window_s`. A
  click after that deadline counts as EXPIRED_UNAPPROVED whatever the wall clock says. The deadline is in memory only,
  with no new persisted field. After a restart the engine holds no proposal, so one left on disk is never executed,
  and it expires by the wall-clock rule with the guard. One stamped days ahead is archived at engine start. Tests:
  tests/test_approval_window_clock.py.
- Attribution results verdicts follow ADR 0022 (2026-10-16, quant review of the results verdicts). The rule was
  recorded before the code, in its own commit. Changes in `goldbot/research/attribution.py`:
  - **Day-clustered errors.** t, `ci95_net` and the new `ci_adj` use standard errors clustered by entry UTC day
    (CR1, `epoch_ns`). Tripling a day's trades no longer raises t.
  - **Row bar.** Every cell carries `t_bar`, `ci_adj` and `verdict_adj`.
    - Breakdown rows use the Bonferroni bar `t_bar = max(2, Φ⁻¹(1 − 0.025/m))`, m = breakdown cells at the minimum,
      read on the row's days − 1 degrees of freedom. The report carries `t_bar` and `m`.
    - The overall cell, the challengers and the live fills use `max(2.0, t⁻¹_{G−1}(0.975))` (F4).
    - `verdict_adj` is signed if and only if `ci_adj` excludes 0.
    - A clustered se of exactly 0 while the trades disperse is "no se": indistinguishable, never a point range (B1).
    - The raw `verdict` (|t| >= 2) is kept for `read_attribution`.
  - **Telegram digest** (`goldbot/telegram/digest.py`, quant ruling F3): names only rows whose `verdict_adj` is
    signed, else "no row clears the bar (|t| ≥ t_bar over m rows) · overall ...".
  - **Live fills** are compared with the backtest's slippage prior, not with the measured table built from the same
    fills. `LiveFills.mean_table_usd` is now `prior_usd`.
  - **Stale note fixed.** The note on live realised R now points at `ClosedTrade.r` in `closed_trades*.jsonl`.

  **Change to the review's formula, ruled correct by the quant reviewer (2026-10-16).** The review's formula (CR0,
  normal quantile) fails the review's own family-wise test: 0.085 in theory, 0.072 over seeds 0–499, against a bar of
  0.07. CR1 with t on G − 1 degrees of freedom gives 0.049. The gates and the stop rule are unchanged.

  Tests: tests/test_attribution.py
  - ::test_rows_bonferroni_fwer, ::test_rows_bonferroni_fwer_with_a_day_effect, ::test_t_bar_values
  - ::test_zero_clustered_se_with_dispersion_is_not_evidence
  - ::test_overall_bar_is_two_or_the_t_quantile_on_days_minus_one_for_overall_challengers_and_live
  - ::test_cell_stats_duplicated_same_day_trades_do_not_raise_t
  - ::test_adjusted_verdict_is_signed_exactly_when_the_adjusted_interval_excludes_zero
  - ::test_live_fills_are_compared_with_the_backtest_slippage_prior_not_the_table_built_from_them
  - ::test_build_report_notes_do_not_say_live_r_unrecorded

- **Engine state keeps moving while the market is closed (2026-10-16; BACKLOG 59; trading-safety and SRE review
  pending).** The engine wrote `engine_<acct>.json` on tick time only. With the market closed the tick stamp is
  frozen, so the file stopped, and health failed `bridge_compat:<acct>` once its `checked_at` was 5 min old: a
  Telegram FAIL and a Healthchecks.io `/fail` every 2 min all weekend, and a FAIL/recovered pair every weekday evening.
  - **The fix.** On the live clock, and only while the session table has the market closed, the engine also writes
    its state when `state_every_s` (10 s) of host time has passed with no write (`Engine._state_heartbeat_due`,
    `_write_heartbeat` in `goldbot/engine/runner.py`). Any write restarts that timer, so the rate stays one per 10 s,
    with the same fsync rules. A host clock stepped back rewrites the file at once in any session (BACKLOG 58: no
    stamp from the future). A session table that cannot be read never takes the heartbeat. Replays and backtests
    (tick clock) are unchanged.
  - **Review HIGH, fixed.** The first version also wrote in market hours, so a quote frozen in an OPEN session kept
    `bridge_compat` OK and `engine` at WARN forever. Now the file ages in market hours as before: `bridge_compat`
    FAILs after 5 min and `engine` after 45 min (`test_a_frozen_feed_in_market_hours_is_never_masked_and_fails_health`).
  - **What the heartbeat does not do.** It reads no account and runs no stage machine, kill switch, weekend rule or
    other exit step. Those stay on the tick-time refresh, as before. It changes no EngineState field, so the gate sees
    exactly what it saw before. No change to the order or exit path; RiskGate untouched.
  - **Fields stay true.** The heartbeat restates `last_tick_age_s`, `tick_ahead_s` and `market_closed` on the host
    clock. On a weekend the file says the last tick is hours old and the market is closed. Before, it kept the last
    market-hours reading. Owner-visible: on a weekend the dashboard's entry status reads the engine's live state, not
    the "engine idle while closed" fallback. It shows only "Market closed": `stale_data` is skipped when the engine
    says the market is closed (`goldbot/api/entry_status.py`), so a weekend never reads like a fault.
  - **The age rules still bite.** Health's rules are unchanged. An engine that writes nothing still FAILs
    `bridge_compat` on the weekend (5 min) and `engine` 45 min after the reopen; `engine_loop` is unchanged.
  - **Backups, checked, left alone.** With no restic keys, `job:backup` and `job:restore_drill` FAIL, which is
    correct until the owner sets the keys; the reason names `goldbot accounts set <key>`. The job check's
    160-character cut (which drops "RUNBOOK 'Backups')") is handled in a separate lane.

- **The digest's "Yesterday" is the opportunity day (2026-10-16; BACKLOG 56, TRACEABILITY V10; code and ui-ux review
  pending).** Before this, the digest's proposals and trades lines covered the UTC calendar day, 00:00-24:00, while
  its month line used the opportunity day. A close at 23:00 UTC was in yesterday's trades and in today's month total.
  Both now use `goldbot/ops/report_days.py`: `day_before(now)` names yesterday and `day_bounds(day)` gives its
  [D-1 22:00, D 22:00) UTC instants. The digest does no day arithmetic of its own, and the month line is built from
  the same day.
  - **What the owner sees.** The header changes from "Yesterday (Thu 15 Oct, 00:00-24:00 UTC)" to
    "Thu 15 Oct trading day (ended 22:00 UTC, 23:00 UK)". The local time comes from `telegram.owner_tz` (default
    Europe/London, shown as "UK"; another zone shows its abbreviation) and is left out only if the zone cannot be
    resolved. With closes at Wed 22:30, Thu 10:00 and Thu 23:00 UTC, the Friday digest
    used to show "Closed 2 trades: net +$30.00 · +0.60R (1 won, 1 lost)" next to "October so far: ... 2 trades ·
    +1.50R". It now shows "Closed 2 trades: net +$80.00 · +1.50R (2 won, 0 lost)", the same trades as the month line.
    The Thu 23:00 close moves to Saturday's digest.
  - **Weekends.** Friday's opportunity day ends at 22:00 UTC, at or after the Friday close in both US DST regimes, so
    Saturday's digest reports Friday. Sunday's day, Sat 22:00 to Sun 22:00 UTC, holds no session: the reopen (22:00
    UTC in summer, 23:00 in winter) opens Monday's day. So Monday's digest says "Trades closed: none" for Sunday, and
    the reopen's closes arrive on Tuesday. Nothing is counted twice or dropped, and Friday is not repeated on Monday.
    A Saturday or Sunday with no proposal and no close shows one line instead of the two "none" lines: "Weekend:
    market closed, no trading. Sunday-evening trades show in Tuesday's digest." A weekend day that has rows (a winter
    Friday close stamped exactly 22:00 UTC is Saturday's) shows them as usual.
  - **Late sends (code review).** "Yesterday" is worked out from the scheduled slot (`DigestSchedule.slot`, passed
    by the bot as `build_digest(as_of=...)`), not from the send time. With `digest_at` 18:00, a send 4.5 h late at
    22:30 used to report the day just ended and the next day's digest reported it again, losing the day before. The
    first line and the expiry of pending proposals still use the send time. The month line now gets the day itself
    (`build_monthly_report(day=...)`). Tested in a summer week, the week US
    DST ends (1 Nov 2026) and a winter week.
  - **Not changed.** The risk line (drawdown, day and week loss against the caps) reads the engine's figures, which

- Heartbeats stamped in the future fail closed (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 58). Before this, a `ts` ahead of the reader's
  clock, or a NaN, made `now - ts > limit` False, so a dead supervisor whose last write carried a fast clock (or came
  from a restored backup) never halted the engines. The shared rule is `goldbot.data.timeutil.heartbeat_problem`:
  a stamp that is not a finite number is `invalid`, one more than a tolerance ahead is `future`, one older than the
  limit is `stale`. Engines halt on `supervisor_heartbeat_future` (more than 5 s ahead, `CLOCK_AHEAD_TOLERANCE_S`)
  or `supervisor_state_unreadable` (a non-numeric or NaN `ts`, or a file that is not an object). The supervisor halts
  every entry on an engine file more than 5 s ahead (`engine_heartbeat_future`, files in `future_engines`; that
  file's currency and money still count). Health fails the supervisor, engine, engine loop, service heartbeat and
  scheduler lines (warns the alert loop) on a stamp more than the same 5 s ahead (`HEALTH_CLOCK_AHEAD_S`), measured
  against max(the pass's `now`, the wall clock) (`checks._base._ahead_s`, SRE review): a pass takes its `now` once
  and can run for minutes while the bridge times out, and a service that beat meanwhile is not a clock fault. The
  later clock can only clear a future flag, never raise one. The Feeds page shows such a supervisor heartbeat as not reporting, the
  dashboard hides combined caps read from it, and a bridge verdict confirmed in the future counts as `unchecked`.
  Left alone on purpose: report-age checks (drift, restore drill, ledger, crossfeed, costs, risk-day roll, re-arm,
  stuck approvals, job overdue), where a future stamp only hides a "report old" warning and the scheduler heartbeat
  still catches a dead producer; the bridge's order age (already refuses either way and on NaN); the tick checks
  (`tick_from_future`); in-process timers (watchdog, dead man's switch, runner timers).
- High-water-mark rises are confirmed (BACKLOG 54, ADR 0018, TRACEABILITY R40; needs trading-safety review). A
  balance read above `balance_closed_hwm` raises it only when the deal history since the mark was set explains it
  (closed deals, commission, swap, deposits; within `risk.hwm_rise_tolerance`, 0.1% of the mark), or when the next
  read agrees. Otherwise the mark stays where it is, the account is read again on the next tick, and the engine
  records `hwm_rise_unconfirmed`, then `hwm_raised` or `hwm_rise_refused`. One inflated balance read no longer
  causes a phantom size-down or kill switch later on. Deposits raise the mark, as before. The mark is never lowered
  (only /rearm resets it). The candidate and the deal-history anchor are stored in core.db (additive migration 2,
  table `hwm_confirmation`), not in a JSON file. A row taken for another mark is void. A restart keeps the candidate
  but never applies it unconfirmed. Health `risk:<account>` warns when a rise has waited more than 5 min in market
  hours, measured from the first of a run of disagreeing candidates. A rollback to an earlier release raises the mark
  on one read again. Review fixes (trading-safety review of faf824c):
  - a candidate that the deals after it carry to a later lower read was a real peak, and the mark rises to it;
  - candidates expire after 10 min;
  - core.db is opened once per engine, with a 500 ms write busy timeout;
  - the paper broker declares its balance reads exact, so one read raises the mark there.
  The ADR is renumbered 0018 (0017 is CostImputer).
- Lane test loop (2026-10-16): lanes iterate on affected tests only with `scripts/lane_test.sh` (pytest-testmon):
  `seed` copies the integrator's `.testmondata` for the lane's base commit from `~/tmp/testmon/<sha>/` (`cp -c`;
  without one the first `iter` runs the full suite), `iter` runs `pytest --testmon -n ${GATES_WORKERS:-2} -q` (never
  with `-m`: testmon turns selection off under `-m`), `final` reminds the lane to run `scripts/gates.sh` once before
  handing back. The integrator runs `refresh` on a clean checkout at the integration tip to (re)build and publish the
  DB for that sha. Rule: lanes iterate with `scripts/lane_test.sh iter`; the full suite (`scripts/gates.sh`) runs once
  before handing back; the integration branch and release run the full gates. Selection is iteration only and
  misses non-Python inputs (config, data files) that testmon does not track, which is why the full gates stay.
- `test_lockout_survives_a_restart` no longer depends on the wall clock (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 55). Root cause: the
  lockout counts `auth_failures` rows by `time.time_ns` and prunes rows older than 15 minutes on every attempt, so a
  run where the wall clock moved 15 minutes between the first failure and the restarted sign-in (a paused VM, a
  starved worker) pruned the five failures, and the sign-in went through ("DID NOT RAISE"). A lock held on aux.db
  past `busy_timeout` was ruled out: it raises `database is locked` and never lets a sign-in through. The test now
  takes the `lockout_clock` fixture (tests/conftest.py: `time.time_ns` pinned, moved only by the test) and restarts
  the store 1 s before the window ends. That makes it stronger: it now fails when the window is halved as well as
  when the failure write is disabled. Evidence: with the lockout clock running 10,000 times faster than real time
  (a scratch pytest plugin), the old test failed 20 of 20 and the new one passed 200 of 200; it also passed 200 of
  200 under CPU stress (load average up to 256). Production code is unchanged: `_reserve` checks and counts in one
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, and no race was found.
  - Follow-up for the test-engineer: the other lockout tests (tests/test_api.py `test_lockout_after_five_failures`,
    `test_one_ip_is_limited_across_many_emails`, tests/test_api_code_lockout.py) still use the wall clock and can
    fail the same way. They can switch to `lockout_clock`.

- **One north-star day for the owner's reports (2026-10-16; TRACEABILITY V9, BACKLOG 57; quant and trading-safety
  review pending).** Before this, the monthly report used the UTC calendar day. The performance report used the
  opportunity day, which rolls at 22:00 UTC. Each had its own day-bucketing and weekday-count code, so a close between
  22:00 and 24:00 UTC landed on different days in the two reports. Both now use `goldbot/ops/report_days.py`
  (`report_day`, `weekdays`, `month_days`, `day_buckets`, `DAY_BOUNDARY`). The one definition of the day,
  `opportunity_day` with `ROLLOVER_UTC_H = 22`, moved from `features/day_type.py` to `goldbot/data/timeutil.py`, next
  to `risk_day`. `day_type` re-exports it, so the features, H-16 and their goldens are unchanged.
  - **The day.** Day D runs from D-1 22:00 UTC to D 22:00 UTC. That time is inside gold's 17:00-18:00 New York break
    in both US DST regimes, so the Sunday reopen counts on Monday and the Friday close on Friday. Tests pin this
    around 22:00 UTC and in the March and November DST weeks (including the US-EU gap week).
  - **Changes the owner will see in the monthly report and the digest's month line.**
    - A close between 22:00 and 24:00 UTC now counts on the next day. That moves best days and £50+ days.
    - The month follows the day too. A close at 23:30 UTC on the month's last day is in the next month's report.
    - The default month is the month of now's opportunity day. At 31 Oct 23:00 UTC that is November.
    - Trading days are the Monday-Friday opportunity days elapsed, today's included.
    - The digest's "month so far" (built at `now - 1 day`) now runs to yesterday's 22:00 UTC roll. A close after the
      roll waits for the next digest.
    - The report's second line now reads "days run from 22:00 UTC the evening before (the opportunity day; the Sunday
      reopen counts on Monday)". "(UTC)" is gone from the title line.
  - **Not changed.** pnl_basis: both reports pick their rows (net only, account currency only) before they bucket
    them, as they did before. The loss caps stay on the risk day (00:00 UTC). So does perf_report's drawdown against
    the limits (`risk_day`, `_risk_week`). No limit, RiskGate check or engine code was touched.
  - **Known gap (digest, not in this lane).** The digest's "Yesterday" line is still the UTC day, 00:00-24:00. A close
    at 23:00 UTC is in yesterday's trades line but in today's month line.
  - **Review follow-ups (quant and trading-safety approved).**
    - ADR 0004 section 6 now records both days: the north-star day is the opportunity day, and the £50 loss limit
      stays on the risk day. DESIGN.md "Time and calendar" now names the reports as users of the fourth day.
    - perf-report's default `--from` is now the first day of the month that holds today's opportunity day. At 31 Oct
      23:00 UTC the default range is 1 Nov to 1 Nov, the month the monthly report shows (`perf_report.default_range`).
    - Before the month's first weekday, the monthly report and the digest show the average per trading day as "n/a"
      (`avg_per_day` None), not £0.00. A winter Friday close at 22:00 UTC lands on the Saturday, for example.
    - The digest's "Yesterday" line is now BACKLOG 56. BACKLOG 57 now says to check each server's
      settings.local.yaml before the validator ships, and to put its error text in the RUNBOOK.
  - **Finding: `risk_day_anchor` is read by no code (for the quant and trading-safety reviewers).**
    - Where it is: `Settings.risk_day_anchor` (`goldbot/config.py:491`) and `config/settings.yaml:7`
      (`{ tz: UTC, time: "00:00" }  # loss caps reset`). No code under goldbot/ or scripts/ reads it, and
      `feature_day_anchor` is unread too (`resample.py` uses its own defaults).
    - Where the 00:00 UTC risk day is actually decided, each place on its own:
      - `timeutil.risk_day` (`goldbot/data/timeutil.py:163`), used by `gate.new_day` (`goldbot/risk/gate.py:537`),
        `throttle.entries_on_day` (`goldbot/risk/throttle.py:83`) and perf_report's drawdown;
      - the engine's own UTC `.date()` shortcut in `_roll_risk_period` (`goldbot/engine/runner.py:2129`);
      - the "resets" time on the entry-status card, `_next_day` (`goldbot/api/entry_status.py:235`);
      - `gate._risk_week`, Sunday 00:00 UTC (`goldbot/risk/gate.py:530`);
      - the supervisor follows the engines through their published `day_start_equity`
        (`goldbot/risk/supervisor.py:156`).
    - Risk today: an owner who sets `risk_day_anchor` in `settings.local.yaml` believes the caps' reset has moved, and
      nothing tells them it has not. If only `risk_day` honoured it, the reset would still happen at 00:00 UTC: the
      runner's `.date()` shortcut returns before `new_day` runs between the anchor and midnight. The card would also
      show the wrong "resets" time, and the perf report's drawdown would disagree with the gate.
    - **Recommendation.**
      1. Now (trading-safety review, BACKLOG 57): pin the setting. A Settings validator should refuse any value other
         than UTC 00:00 at load, saying the risk day is fixed. That only tightens, and it is safe on rollback (an older
         release ignores the key). `tests/test_report_days.py::test_the_configured_risk_day_anchor_is_the_hard_coded_risk_day`
         already pins the shipped yaml.
      2. Do not honour it piecemeal. Moving the risk day to the 22:00 UTC roll would stop one Asia session's losses
         being split across two caps at midnight. But it changes every daily-cap reset. It needs one shared
         risk-day function for all five places above, a migration for the persisted `_last_reset`, and an owner
         decision with a trading-safety review. Do it only if the quant reviewer finds the midnight split matters in
         measured trades.
    - A regression test pins today's behaviour: `new_day` does not reset at 22:30 UTC and does at 00:00.
  - Tests: tests/test_report_days.py (new, 17 cases). tests/test_monthly_report.py: 2 replaced, 3 new.
    tests/test_currency_followups.py: `account_month` now takes its first and last opportunity days as YYYY-MM-DD.

  telegram, news). The commands live in goldbot/ops/commands/, one module per area, and each registers its handler

  services/_base.py), so `patch("goldbot.ops.run.x")` still takes effect. Importing run.py still loads no third-party
  package, which matters for the Wine bridge. Tests: tests/test_ops_run_cli_golden.py was captured before the split. It
  pins the usage text, every side-effect-free `--help`, which function each command reaches and with which arguments,

  registry order, the re-exports and the call-through rule.
- Round-trip costs in the daily £ projection (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 36, trading-safety review LOW-6). Accounts with
  an absolute daily loss limit (icm-demo, £50) now refuse an entry when loss so far (+ open risk) + stop risk + round
  trip > the limit. Before, the round trip was left out. The round trip has two parts, both x lots x contract x fx in
  the account currency:
  - spread, slippage and commission: `cost_atr` x ATR, the engine's `_cost_atr` (the nightly cost table, else
    `cost_atr: 0.10`);
  - the paid swap, when a broker rollover falls before 00:00 UTC.

  The swap reuses ADR 0017's rule. `cost_imputation.account_swap` takes the table's measured rates, else the settings
  prior. `paid_swap_per_oz` counts the triple day and never counts a credit. The closed-trade charge now calls the same
  two helpers. The projection can only grow: a negative cost or a credit counts as 0, and a NaN swap refuses
  (`invalid:swap_usd_per_oz`). The approval re-check prices the swap again at the click. No other check reads the
  cost, and exits are untouched. Worked example at £5,000 GBP (fx 0.75, ATR $10, 0.01 lot): stop £7.50, round trip
  £0.30, one night of the -$60 prior £0.45 (£1.35 on Wednesday). With £42 lost, the projection was £49.50 (allowed)
  and is now £50.25 (refused). New `GateDecision.cost_amount` and `Intent.swap_usd_per_oz` (in-memory only, nothing
  persisted). Tests: tests/test_projection_costs.py; three older boundary pins moved by exactly the cost.

  Trading-safety review fixes (one MEDIUM, four LOW):
  - A NaN swap rate no longer reads as "pays nothing". `SwapSpec` and the cost table's swap fields are finite-only,
    so a NaN table fails to load and the prior is charged. A NaN broker reading becomes "no swap" in the nightly job.
    If a non-finite rate still reaches the engine, `_swap_usd_per_oz` returns NaN and the gate refuses.
  - A swap that cannot be priced at the click refuses the approval (`swap_unavailable`).
  - The spread is counted twice on purpose: `cost_atr` includes it, and so does the stop risk measured from the fill.
    This is conservative and recorded in the gate comment and R42.
  - Quant, code and trading-safety reviews done.
- Trial registry push re-checks the release asset just before the swap (2026-10-16, BACKLOG 51). The VPS monthly loop
  pushes `research-v1/registry.jsonl` outside the workflows' `concurrency: research-registry`, so a workflow save
  that landed between the loop's pull and its push was overwritten, and the other way round too. Both writers now run
  one implementation: `goldbot.research.registry_sync`, over HTTP on the VPS and through `gh` in the workflows.
  `scripts/registry_release.sh fetch | save | recover` is a thin wrapper over it. Each save is a compare-and-swap:
  - Note the asset's stamp (id, updated_at, size, digest) at the pull.
  - Upload the merged rows as `registry.jsonl.pending-*`.
  - Re-read the stamp, then delete the pulled asset by its id.
  - Rename the pending asset, then re-read: published means our id is the lowest-id `registry.jsonl`, with the
    deleted id filtered out. The rename's status code is not relied on. A re-read that still lists the deleted id,
    or does not list our upload, is stale and is read again after a wait; our upload is never dropped on one.

  Downloads are by asset id (`gh api -H 'Accept: application/octet-stream' .../releases/assets/<id>`), and every
  `gh` call times out after 120 s. `recover` prints what each copy adds (row count and trial keys) before it
  publishes.

  Another writer is detected by a changed stamp, a 404 on the delete, or another copy being published at the rename.
  The pending upload is then dropped, and the writer waits a jittered 0.5-1.5 s per attempt, pulls, merges and
  retries, at most 3 times. After that it fails loudly. On the VPS, `registry_sync` records `failed: ...` and the
  loop carries on; in a workflow the job fails. The local file keeps every union it saw, so a lost race drops no
  row. The keyed union counts each trial once in the deflated Sharpe.

  Once the old asset is deleted, the pending upload is never deleted unless another copy is published. If the rename
  keeps failing, the upload stays and the save fails with "run `scripts/registry_release.sh recover`". `recover`
  unions every `registry.jsonl` and `registry.jsonl.pending-*` on the release and publishes the result the same way.
  Reads never start from an empty registry when the release exists, in two cases:
  - a pending upload with no published copy (a writer mid-swap, or stranded);
  - a release with no `registry.jsonl` at all, unless `--bootstrap` is passed.

  The refusal of a union shorter than the published copy is kept, and the VPS applies it too. `--clobber` is no
  longer used. GitHub has no conditional upload, so the re-check alone is not atomic with the delete; the delete by
  id and the post-rename re-read are what keep that window safe. A writer outside this protocol (a manual
  `gh release upload --clobber`) is still not protected against.

  Rollback: a pre-51 VPS release reads a pending-only release as an empty registry and its push deletes and
  re-uploads `registry.jsonl` directly. Do not roll the VPS back while a pending asset is stranded; run `recover`
  first.

  Tests: tests/test_registry_push_race.py and tests/test_registry_release.py. They cover another writer landing
  after the upload, before the delete and during the rename; a rename that fails, or answers 200 without renaming;
  two protocol writers interleaved, including the first-ever push; a failed re-check; recover; bootstrap; and the
  bounded-retry failure.

  - Needs security and trading-safety review.
- Open-risk heat cap and open-risk daily projection (2026-10-11, BACKLOG 19 playbook G-4 and BACKLOG 35 review
  MEDIUM-4, row R38; **both off by default**; needs trading-safety review). The engine computes, on every account
  refresh, each open position's remaining stop risk (max(0, loss from the current close price to its SL) x lots x
  contract x the broker's conversion, account currency; `goldbot/risk/open_risk.py`) and the positions per side, and
  publishes `open_risk` (null = unknown), `open_risk_positions`, `open_long`, `open_short`, `limits.heat` and
  `limits.project_open_risk` in engine_<account>.json. `risk.heat: {enabled: false, max_open_risk: 0.02,
  max_same_direction: 2}`: RiskGate refuses `heat_cap` when open risk + the new trade's stop risk > 2% of equity and
  `same_direction_cap` at the third same-side position on the account (any agent, or the owner). `risk.project_open_risk:
  false`: when true and the account has `daily_loss_limit_abs`, the daily projection adds the open risk. A position
  without SL, on another symbol, or without a usable conversion makes the open risk unknown: `open_risk_unknown` while
  either rule is on (fail closed). Exits never consult any of it. Owner: settings.local.yaml `risk: { heat: { enabled:
  true, ... }, project_open_risk: true }`, restart the engine. Not done: the cross-account sum and count (the
  supervisor does not publish open risk or side counts yet), health lines and the dashboard budget (ui-ux).
- Auto entries at one bar close each see the previous fill (2026-10-11, trading-safety review HIGH on BACKLOG 19,
  pre-existing; row R38). Before, in auto mode every entry decided at one bar close was checked against the account as
  read before the first one filled, so `max_positions`, the combined cap, the heat cap and the same-direction cap could
  each be passed within a bar close (propose mode was safe: the approval re-check reads afresh). Now
  `Engine._after_auto_order` re-reads the account after each auto order (`_refresh_account` on the broker's last
  tick); a fill the positions read does not show yet is added conservatively (one more position on its side, its
  lots, the gate's margin, its stop risk); an ambiguous result (neither a fill nor a definite reject,
  `DEFINITE_REJECT_RETCODES`) or a failed re-read stops auto entries for the rest of that bar close, journalled as
  `auto_paused:unconfirmed_order` / `auto_paused:account_unread`. Two timeframes closing together share it.
  Re-verification LOW-B: an auto entry that did not fill is journalled `auto_rejected:<retcode>` (definite reject,
  nothing placed) or `auto_unconfirmed:<retcode>`, never `executed:auto`; 10032 (only real accounts) and 10046 (hedge
  prohibited) joined `DEFINITE_REJECT_RETCODES`, now an explicit list of defined codes (review LOW-1: undefined codes such as 10037 or 10047 are ambiguous). LOW-C: a `place_order` that raises (bridge timeout, terminal error)
  no longer aborts the bar close: auto entries pause for it (`_auto_paused = (close, "order_raised")`), the error is
  counted through `note_tick_error` (entries blocked until a clean decision bar), the decision is journalled
  `auto_unconfirmed:<ExceptionType>`, and its pending_orders row stays `sending`, so it is never re-sent and a position
  that did open is picked up by reconciliation (adopted in this engine's magic range) or by the restart check.
  Review MEDIUM-2 (of 2c1935f): that `sending` row used to survive the adoption, so a restart recovered the send again
  and replaced the adopted trade (stop back to the entry stop, bars_held and scaled reset), after which the exit
  policy could send a stop looser than the broker's. Now (a) `_adopt` marks a matching unfilled row filled with its
  position and `_reconcile` saves; (b) `_resolve_sent` (shared by `_load_orders` and the in-process path) keeps a trade
  the open table already holds and only marks its row filled (`reconcile_sent_known`); (c) `_manage_policies` sends a
  modify only when the new stop is tighter than both the engine's and the broker's (side-aware; a looser engine copy is
  raised to the broker's); (d) `_resolve_stale_sending` resolves rows still `sending` after `SENDING_RESOLVE_S` (60 s)
  in `_reconcile`, from the same positions and deals lookup (tests/test_sending_row_recovery.py: raise, adopt, tighten,
  restart; no looser modify; bars_held and scaled kept; shorts; the control still tightens).
- Open-risk review LOWs (2026-10-11, row R38): LOW-1 a failure computing the open risk sets it unknown and never
  aborts the account refresh, and a failed account read at the bar close no longer skips `_manage_open` (exits still
  run, then the error propagates and no entry is decided on that close: the base branch's review-L3 rule, kept at the
  merge); LOW-2 `AccountState.open_risk` defaults to unknown
  (None) until the engine has read the positions; LOW-3 health `open_risk:<account>` warns and tells the owner on
  Telegram (`NOTIFY_ON_WARN`) while the open risk is unknown and the heat cap, or the projection with an absolute limit,
  is on; LOW-4 "per account vs combined same-side count" is an owner decision in OWNER_GUIDE section 4.
- MT5 adapter reports the position ticket, not the deal ticket (2026-10-11, trading-safety re-verification MEDIUM-A):
  `place_order` returned `position_id=res.deal`, but an MT5 position's ticket is its opening ORDER's, so the engine
  keyed `self.open` by a number the terminal never lists (a phantom close at the next sweep, the real position adopted
  as an orphan). `mt5_adapter._position_ticket` now reads the order's deals (`history_deals_get(ticket=res.order)`:
  MT5's `ticket=` selects by ORDER, review MEDIUM-1) and takes `position_id` from the deal whose ticket is `res.deal`
  (right on netting accounts too), else falls back to `res.order`; an older order numbered like the fill's deal is
  never taken. The terminal account must also be **hedging**: `AccountInfo.margin_mode` (MT5 ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_*)
  and `accounts.verify_terminal_account` refuse netting, exchange or an unreported mode at start, on every order and in
  preflight, since fills on a netting account join one position per symbol. An older bridge does not report the mode,
  so **update the MT5 bridge before the brain** or the engine refuses to start (open positions keep their broker
  stops). Bridge protocol v4 (`API_VERSION = 4`, `MIN_COMPATIBLE = 3`; a v3 brain ignores the new field). Tests on a fake terminal whose deal and
  order tickets differ (tests/test_mt5_position_ticket.py, including the engine keying and a sweep + reconcile that
  keep the trade). **Verify on the demo terminal:** after the first demo fill, the engine's `open` position id and the
  `adopt_orphan` count in the decisions journal (expected: the terminal's position ticket, no orphan adopted).
- Broker ledger: closes finance audit GAP-07 and GAP-08 (row X19, ADR 0015). A new daily scheduler job,
  `broker_ledger` (23:25 UTC), only reads the broker. Per account it stores in aux.db (migration 7, additive):
  - a balance, equity, margin and currency snapshot, stamped with the real read time and keyed by the slot's day;
  - the deposits, withdrawals, credit and adjustments taken from the MT5 balance deals. A baseline day books them
    flagged `baseline`; operations after a cancelled deal are tagged `follows_cancel`.

  It ties the balance out against the deals after the previous snapshot. The deal cursor stays within a day of the
  read, so an idle account never drifts into a new baseline. An unexplained balance is read again once, 5 s later,
  before it FAILs. It also reconciles closed records and open trades with the broker by position id, reporting
  missing, extra and mismatched positions.

  The health check `reconcile:<account>` is now the worse of the D12 feed report and the ledger report: a trade
  difference warns, an unexplained balance change fails, any aux.db error other than a missing table warns, and the
  reason gives counts only. The owner reads the amounts with `python -m goldbot.ops.ledger show <account>`
  (read-only). No bridge or protocol change: `deals_since` already carries the balance deals.
- Conflict-free docs (2026-10-11, ADR 0012; speed-up review items 1-2): HANDOFF.md, docs/TRACEABILITY.md and
  docs/BACKLOG.md are now generated by `scripts/docs_assemble.py` from one file per change: `docs/handoff.d/`
  (dated bullets, newest first), `docs/traceability.d/` (one YAML per row; counts computed) and `docs/backlog.d/`
  (one file per item; the table is ordered by `rank`). The migration was mechanical: rendering reproduces the
  old files byte for byte, apart from a "generated" comment on line 1. TRACEABILITY still has 212 rows (179
  implemented, 16 partial, 3 missing, 6 deviates, 8 in review). New ids come from `new-row R` and `new-item`; a
  clash is caught by the `docs-assemble` pre-commit hook (which CI runs) and fixed by `fix-ids`. Lanes are merged
  with `scripts/docs_assemble.py merge <branch>`, which also absorbs branches that still edit the old rendered
  files. Never edit the rendered files.
- **Outside dead man's switch and a hash-pinned MT5 box (SRE, 2026-10-11; first-deploy risks 1 and 2).**
  - Alerts no longer depend only on the brain. After each health pass, the Telegram service pings a Healthchecks.io
    check (free tier; ADR 0014, `goldbot/ops/deadman.py`). It sends an ok ping every `telegram.deadman_every_min`
    (2) min while health has no FAIL, and `<url>/fail` (body: failing check names only) on a FAIL or an undelivered
    Telegram alert. The URL is keyring-only (`goldbot accounts set deadman-url`) and never logged. When it is unset,
    nothing is sent and health `deadman` WARNs. Owner steps: first-deploy.md P7 and 8b, RUNBOOK section 6 "Outside
    alert". Tests: `tests/test_deadman.py`.
  - The Wine MT5 box's Windows-Python packages come from `goldbot/ops/linux/mt5-bridge-requirements.txt`. The file
    is rendered from uv.lock by `scripts/bridge_requirements.py` (CPython 3.11 win_amd64 wheels, sha256) and
    installed with `pip install --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary :all:`. pip is no longer upgraded and goldbot
    is no longer built editable (a `.pth` instead). goldbot-deploy reinstalls the packages when uv.lock changes, with
    the bridges stopped. CI check: `tests/test_bridge_requirements.py`. An existing MT5 box moves onto the file once,
    by hand (RUNBOOK 0.5).
- Decider identity kept out of approval files and the API (BACKLOG 52, TRACEABILITY A14; 2026-10-11).
  - `Proposal` no longer has `decided_by` / `decided_via`, so `approvals/done/` files record only `decided_channel`
    and `decided_ts`. Older files that still carry the fields load normally (they are not counted as schema skew),
    and their identity is dropped as they are read.
  - API contract change: `DecidedProposal.decided_by` is replaced by `decided_channel` and `decided_ts`. The
    dashboard's decided cards say "via Telegram" or "via the dashboard" and no longer show an email.
  - Identity for audit: dashboard decisions are already in the auth audit log (`decision`, with the email).
    Telegram decisions have no identity record anywhere now, because only allow-listed ids can decide.
  - Still on disk: the short-lived `approvals/decisions/<id>.json` keeps `by` ("dashboard:<email>" or
    "telegram:<id>") until the engine archives the proposal (the next tick). Proposed as a follow-up.
  - Needs security and trading-safety review.
- Email sign-in link, security re-verify nits on 1a8bf43. `auth.mail.dashboard_origin` now refuses any
  whitespace, control character, `\` or `;`, and an empty host. It is stored as the normalised lower-case
  `scheme://netloc`. `coarse_ip` gives the IPv4 /16 for an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (`::ffff:203.0.113.45` ->
  `203.0.x.x`).
- Email sign-in link: follow-ups to the security review of fe58fae (approved; no timing oracle found).
  - M1: ADR 0013 records the accepted risk (with mail on, mailbox plus authenticator signs the owner in) and its
    limits. Every `email_link_login` sends the owner a Telegram notice (`_notify_owner`) and an email
    (`sign_in_notice_message`), with no token and only a coarse network hint (`auth.coarse_ip`: IPv4 /16, IPv6 /32).
  - L1: `auth.mail.dashboard_origin` is checked with `urlsplit`: https with a host and no user info, path, query or
    fragment; http only for exactly localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1.
  - L2: sign-out-everywhere (`revoke_sessions`) and the server's `revoke-sessions` command also delete email links,
    in the same transaction.
  - L3: new health check `email_link` warns when the owner's address hit the hourly limit 3 or more times in 24 h
    (`email_link_health_note`, never names the address). OWNER_GUIDE says what to do when no link arrives.
  - L4: `web/src/main.tsx` takes link tokens out of the address bar at start, signed in or not.
  - L5: `SmtpMailer.ready()` is cached for 60 s (`READY_CACHE_S`).
  - UX: a failed redeem goes straight to "Email me a sign-in link" (the old link is spent).
  - RUNBOOK: aux.db schema 6 cannot be stepped back to 4. Releases since state-store step 3 open it; older ones are
    refused by the deploy.
- Engine loop heartbeat and watchdogs (2026-10-11, SRE first-deploy risk). A hung engine used to show only after 45
  minutes. Now each loop pass writes `state/heartbeat_engine-<account>.json`, with or without ticks
  (goldbot/ops/watchdog.py `LoopWatch`). Health check `engine_loop:<account>` FAILs after 150 s.
  goldbot-engine@.service is `Type=notify` with `WatchdogSec=300`, so systemd restarts a stuck loop, and the
  restart reconciles with the broker as usual. On the MT5 box, `goldbot-bridge-watchdog@.timer` restarts a bridge
  that stops answering `GET /health`. Hosts set up earlier need the units reinstalled, then the rollback floor set
  to this commit: RUNBOOK "Engine loop stuck, and the watchdogs". Tests: tests/test_engine_watchdog.py.
- Equity confirmation before the 12% kill switch (BACKLOG 44, ADR 0016, TRACEABILITY R39; revised after the
  trading-safety review of d2f2999; needs trading-safety re-review). A 12% equity read trips at once when the balance
  plus the profit and swap of every position on the account agrees within 2% of the high-water mark
  (`risk.equity_check_tolerance`). Otherwise it starts a sticky pending state: entries are refused
  `equity_unconfirmed`, no stage moves, the account is re-read on the next tick, and any later 12% read trips. Pending
  clears only after 60 s of reads below 10% (`risk.equity_recovery_s`) and survives a restart. One bad read (0 or
  collapsed) no longer closes every position at market. Exits are never gated; broker stops keep resting meanwhile.
  Bridge protocol v5 (`account_positions`, `Position.swap`): deploy the MT5 box first, then the brain (entries pause
  until both run v5). A risk-state save that fails (a full disk) on the account refresh is logged and blocks
  entries (`tick_error`) but never raises, so it can no longer stop, delay or narrow the kill switch (re-review
  MEDIUM-1, LOW-2). Follow-up: BACKLOG 53 (confirm high-water-mark rises).
- The record now carries what the monthly finance audit needs (2026-10-11, docs/finance/audit-framework.md gaps
  GAP-01/02/03/04/05/10/13; TRACEABILITY X18). `ClosedTrade` gains `decision_price`, `decision_spread_points` and
  `decision_utc` (the signal, from the proposal) next to `requested_price` (the quote the order was priced from: in
  propose mode the quote at the owner's approval), so side x (requested - decision) is the cost of the 90 s wait;
  `timeframe`, `family` and `model_version` (the agent's champion registry version); `initial_sl`, `final_sl`,
  `final_tp`; `money_source` (broker | engine) and `pnl_basis`, "gross" unless commission and swap are both known, so
  a fallback record is never summed as net. The entry facts travel as `EntryAudit` on the pending order and the open
  trade, so a restart or a recovered fill keeps them. Exit legs (engine closes, the scale-out, broker stop and target
  fills against their level) go to a new store table `exit_fills`, kept apart from `fills` so the entry slippage
  table is unchanged; the legs are buffered in memory and written by `_flush_closed` after the tick's exits, so an
  exit never waits on a file write (a failed write keeps them for the next flush). The archived proposal keeps
  `decided_ts` and `decided_channel` ("telegram" | "dashboard", no id), taken by `bus.archive` from the decision file
  for approved or rejected proposals only (a stale one archived on restart takes none; an unreadable file is "no
  decision"). The paper broker's deals now say `swap` None (not modelled), so paper records are gross. The journal
  `order` row now names its proposal (GAP-12). Every new field defaults to unknown (ADR 0010). Not done: the monthly
  report and digest do not yet read `pnl_basis` (PR-1 must exclude "gross" rows from net), no health count of gross
  records, no fx on the record (GAP-06), no broker reconciliation (GAP-08). The existing `decided_by` /
  `decided_via` still keep the Telegram id and dashboard email in approvals/done on the VPS: BACKLOG 52.
  Tests: tests/test_finance_audit_record.py.
- First demo deploy (SRE, 2026-10-11): `docs/deploy/first-deploy.md` is the owner's 60-90 min session (case A, fresh
  install). The brain runs on Oracle Ampere A1, now **2 OCPU / 12 GB**, the Always Free total since mid-2026 (it was
  4 / 24). MT5 runs on a bridge box. Day 1 tries both bridge options:
  - A: an Azure B2ats v2 Windows VM, set up with `vps_bootstrap.ps1 -BridgeOnly`. It runs one bridge service as the
    non-admin user `goldbot-bridge`, with admin-only ACLs, a signed MT5 installer and machine-wide Python. The brain
    reaches it over Tailscale through its SSH tunnel; the tunnel key has a forced no-op command.
  - B: an Oracle micro running MT5 under Wine (`mt5_bootstrap.sh`, 4 GB swap).

  Keep whichever bridge is stable for 24 h. Both bootstraps take an owner-checked 40-hex commit, run from a hash-checked
  download, and keep going if SSH drops. Python packages come from `uv.lock` (`uv sync --frozen`; `goldbot-deploy`
  too, after its root copy is reinstalled). The MT5 account must be a hedging demo (bridge v4). Paid fallback, the
  owner's decision: a 2-4 GB Windows VPS with the full install.

  Follow-ups: Cloudflare Tunnel with Access; an outside dead man's switch (alerts come only from the brain); a
  main-loop engine heartbeat (a hung engine shows as stale only after 45 min).
- **Monthly report and daily digest: net means net (2026-10-11; finance audit GAP-05, quant review pending).**
  Before this, `goldbot/ops/monthly_report.py` and `goldbot/telegram/digest.py` added every closed trade's P&L into
  "net", including rows whose commission and swap were never recorded. They now use the same rule as
  `perf_report.py`. The rule lives in one place, `gates_phase.pnl_basis`; `perf_report` imports it from there.
  - **Net figures use net rows only.** A net row has `pnl_basis` "net", or is a legacy row that records both
    commission and swap. This covers money, R, the chained return, drawdown, best days, £50+ days, the average per
    trading day and the digest's won/lost count.
  - **Every other row is shown apart and summed as gross.** That is `pnl_basis` "gross", or a legacy row without both
    costs. The wording is "N trades gross only (costs not recorded)", with the gross money and R. The monthly report
    adds "left out of every figure above", the month-so-far line adds "not summed", and a day with only gross rows
    says "net not recorded". No gross figure carries the word net.
  - **Change the owner will see.** Trades from the engine's own fills, where no broker deals were read, have
    `money_source` "engine" and no costs. They now show as gross only and leave the net totals. So do legacy records
    from before the closed-trade record carried commission and swap. Net totals can therefore drop compared with
    yesterday's digest.
  - **Day convention, stated in the report.** A day is the UTC calendar day, 00:00-24:00. That is the risk day on
    which the loss caps reset (`risk_day_anchor`) and the digest's "yesterday" (`MonthlyReport.day_boundary`, the
    report's second line). `perf_report` uses the opportunity day, which rolls at 22:00 UTC, so a close between 22:00
    and 24:00 UTC falls on different days in the two reports. We kept the UTC day so that the monthly £50 days line up
    with the daily loss cap and the digest.
  - **New health check `pnl_basis:<account>`.** It WARNs when more than 20% of the account's closed trades over the
    last 30 days (by exit) are not net (`PNL_BASIS_GROSS_WARN_PCT`, `PNL_BASIS_WINDOW_DAYS`). It never FAILs, even
    on an unreadable record, and it does not notify on WARN. Why 20%: past one trade in five, the net totals cover
    too little of the month's trading to be read as its result. The usual cause is an unreadable broker deal history
    (check the bridge).
  - **Not changed (flagged for the quant reviewer).** `gates_phase` (the phase gates and the stop rule's loss
    series), `research/ruin.py` and `ops/ledger.py` still read every row's `pnl` without regard to its basis. The
    phase gate is out of bounds for this change.
  - Tests: tests/test_monthly_report.py (6 new), tests/test_digest.py (2 new), tests/test_health.py (6 new). Net
    fixtures in tests/test_currency_followups.py, tests/test_excursion.py and tests/test_sizing_review_fixes.py now say
    `pnl_basis="net"`. Two sizing-review assertions on engine-fill trades now expect those trades as gross only.
- Owner-only email sign-in link and clearer sign-in screens (owner request 2026-10-11; TRACEABILITY U20). The login
  page now titles each flow (Sign in, Reset your password, Email me a sign-in link, Finish signing in, Set a new
  password), shows **Forgot password?**, **Email me a sign-in link** (only when the server has mail configured) and
  **Use a recovery code**, and fits a phone (16px inputs, 44px targets). `POST /api/auth/email-link {email}` answers
  one generic 200 for every address; it mails a link only to `auth.owner_email` (trimmed, case-insensitive) when that
  account is the enabled owner and mail is configured. Token: `token_urlsafe(32)`, SHA-256 in aux.db `email_links`
  (migration 6, additive), single use, 15 min; at most 3 requests an hour per address and per IP
  (`email_link_requests`). `POST /api/auth/email-link/redeem {token, totp}` STILL needs the authenticator code; any
  redeem of a live link deletes every outstanding link (a wrong code burns it and counts towards the sign-in lockout;
  unknown tokens count against the IP only). A password change, forgot-password or recovery-code sign-in also
  deletes outstanding links. Mail: `goldbot/api/mailer.py`, smtplib + STARTTLS, settings `auth.mail` (real values in
  settings.local.yaml), password in the keyring as `smtp-password`; sent in a background task after the response,
  failures logged and audited by exception type only. `goldbot run mail-test` checks the setup. Rollback note: aux.db
  schema 6 is additive, so every release since state-store step 3 opens it; a release from before step 3 is refused
  by the deploy (no 6 -> 4 step-back yet). Needs security review.
- **Owner history: security and quant review fixes to bd5324e (2026-10-11, M43).** The `no-mt5-report` hook now
  catches the following, whatever the file is called:
  - a CSV with a UTF-8 BOM (Excel "CSV UTF-8");
  - the analyser's private markdown, by its title line, and its JSON summary, by both of its source keys;
  - a gzip, decompressed up to 20 MB;
  - a zip, by each member's name and by each member's content within the byte budget. Archives are opened one
    level deep.

  Refusal messages show only `~/Personal project/trade-history`, never a path. `main` turns both refusals into a
  plain exit. `.share.md` now states how the USD conversion was found ("implied by N trades" / "assumed 1.0"),
  never the rate. The module docstring records the rule: nothing that multiplies with USD/oz into an amount (lots,
  ounces, the rate) may enter `.share.md`.
- **Owner history: shareable summary, in-repo input refused, hook covers every input format (2026-10-11; owner
  approved the owner-method study, M43).** `python -m goldbot.ops.run owner-history` now refuses a report inside any
  git work tree before opening it, and prints only the shareable summary (`render_share`, also written as
  `owner_history_*.share.md`): win rate, mean R or net USD/oz, holding-time quantiles, session/hour/weekday/side/
  holding histograms with each slice's verdict against the Bonferroni bar, winning and losing streaks, drawdown %,
  risk per trade and leverage relative to equity, and K. No account identifier, ticket or account-currency amount;
  the money figures stay in the private `.md`. The `no-mt5-report` hook now also rejects an English MT5 Positions /
  Orders / Deals header row in CSV, TSV, HTML or xlsx (any trade count, any stamp format) and the analyser's own
  outputs. Not built: a separate `scripts/owner_history.py` (the entry point already exists; a second one would
  drift). Needs quant and security review.
- **Performance report: quant review fixes (2026-10-11; follow-up to 207c9ef, re-review pending).**
  `goldbot/ops/perf_report.py` reads the record's finance-audit fields when present: `pnl_basis`, `money_source`,
  `family`, `timeframe`, `model_version` and `decision_price`.
  - **Net and gross columns.** Only `pnl_basis` "net" rows go into the net columns, plus legacy rows that record
    both commission and swap. Gross rows go into the gross column and count as "net not recorded (gross only, N)".
    Other rows count as "basis not recorded". Readings, money per day, the north star and drawdown use net rows
    only.
  - **Shadow table.** It reports `sum_r` (gross), and every reading is marked "(gross)". Matching ignores `taken`,
    which becomes its own column. The model version comes from the trade's closed record (see the
    re-verify bullet). Every unmatched proposal says why.
  - **Calibration row.** It sets the approved signals' shadow R (gross) against their live net R. The closed trade
    is linked by client order id = proposal id.
  - **Limits.** They are grouped by the RiskGate's windows: the risk day from 00:00 UTC and the risk week from
    Sunday 00:00 UTC. The section is labelled "closed-trade, lower bound" and points to a future daily risk summary.
  - **North star.** It selects trades by their entry's opportunity day, whenever they closed. Open trades entered
    on an opportunity day show as pending (from `state/orders_<account>.json`). Day types are labelled "(ex post)".
    The bars come from one source, `--bars-source` (default dukascopy).
  - **Samples.** A row is sufficient only from 30 trades with a net R. The header gives the group count and a
    multiple-comparisons caveat. Entry slippage comes from `decision_price`.
  - Tests: `tests/test_perf_report.py` (37), including the 22:00 boundary, several shadow versions with an untaken
    candidate, a trade straddling the range end, and the day's own range left out of its ATR.
- **Performance report: the model version comes from the closed record (2026-10-11; quant re-verify of a4e532f).**
  The record lane writes `model_version` on the closed-trade record (EntryAudit), linked by client order id =
  proposal id, not on the proposal.
  - An approved proposal that became a trade is matched to the shadow version named on its record.
  - Rejected and expired proposals, and approved ones without a record or a version, match the nearest p. The table
    labels them "version inferred (nearest p)", with a count per outcome.
  - The report now reads the typed `ClosedTrade` fields. The raw-JSON reader (`load_closed_trade_rows`) is gone, so
    `gates_phase.load_closed_trades` is unchanged from main.

- Shadow book (`engine/shadow.py`): the engine on the canonical-cost broker (IC Markets) paper-trades the champion and
  every challenger on live bars with label-identical mechanics (exact parity with `triple_barrier` is tested) and
  writes `state/shadow_<version>.json`; the Saturday job promotes/retires from it, and the daily `model_watch` job runs
  a CUSUM on a new champion's first two weeks and restores the previous champion on an alarm.
- Population tournament (`research/population.py`, weekly `tournament` job): agents = specialist family + config with
  lineage; founders seeded per family; fitness only from shadow trades (per-trade Sharpe x calibration x drawdown
  haircut x diversity penalty); ranked after 60 trades; retired on a negative 80% lower bound after 100 trades or two
  bottom-quartile months (then 6 months more in shadow); shadow -> live via DSR with population size as trials;
  winners cloned into 2-3 mutated shadow children; caps 12 live / 24 shadow; capital = family weight x fitness share.
  Models are keyed by agent (`ModelRegistry`); the engine trades only live members and shadow-trades all of them;
  `state/agents.json` feeds the dashboard's Agents league table.
- Journal + staff agents: the engine journals every decision to the store's `decisions` table. `goldbot/agents/`:

  Opus 5.5 through a budgeted tool-use loop over read-only tools (`agents/tools.py`; the only write is filing a

  (`settings.yaml: agents`), every run logged to `state/agent_runs.jsonl`; reports appear on the Agents screen.
  The research analyst (Saturdays, after the improvement agent) turns filed hypotheses into at most two bounded
  walk-forward trials per run (`run_trial`: numeric overrides within +-50% of the defaults, recorded in the trial

  explains `execution/audit.py`'s numbers: slippage per session/order type against the nightly cost table with drift
  flags, widened spreads, failed orders.
- Research director (`research/director.py`, scheduler job `research_director` Saturdays 12:30 UTC, before
  `agents_weekly`): a deterministic score per family from the trial registry (median OOF AUC z-score with
  se = 1/sqrt(3 n_oof), best DSR on 200+ model-filtered trades, lookahead flags) and the shadow book/population
  (shadow t-stat), then splits what is left of the quarter's trial budget (`research.trial_budget_quarter`, 20 when
  unset, counted from the registry): an exploration floor (`research.director_floor`) per family, the rest in
  proportion to evidence, 0 for a lookahead-dirty family; the label grid may use at most half of a family's share.
  Trials with status `holdout` are never evidence and `monthly_research` never walks into the held-out year
  (`research.holdout_from`, default 2025-10-01). Output `state/research_plan.json`; `monthly_research` follows it (flat
  budget without a plan under 21 days old) and stops when the quarter's budget is spent. The `research_director` staff
  agent explains the plan (`read_research_plan`) and may file two hypotheses; the analyst prefers the plan's focus
  families. Boundary: it decides what to research, never what is promoted or traded; promotion stays with the gates.
  Two more inputs (2026-10-10, revised after the quant review): (1) the daily attribution report
  (`state/attribution.json`): the director rebuilds each family's cell from the report's per-trade rows, counting only
  trades entered on or after their model version's promotion (model registry; an unpromoted version counts nothing),
  from a report dated at or before the plan and at most 14 days old; under `attribution.min_trades` is noise. The
  net-R t-stat is shrunk by n/(n+100), clipped to +-1 at t = 3, and tilts the evidence share of the pool by at most
  +-25%, only for a family with no shadow t-stat (the same shadow trades are never counted twice; the
  `director_floor` is never tilted). (2) Retired families are governance in settings, `research.retired_families`
  (family, hypothesis id, retired date, reason, registry trials); `docs/research/hypotheses.md` section B mirrors it,
  a test checks they agree, and the plan stores the doc's sha256 and any drift (`hypotheses_drift`) but the doc never
  moves a trial. The retired families SHARE one exploration trial a quarter (none once any of them had a trial this
  quarter; after the live families' floors), given to the clean retired family with the best positive
  post-retirement attribution, else by a deterministic rotation over quarters (`retired_explore` in the plan); each
  is reinstated only by attribution trades after its retirement date with shrunk t >= 2
  Bonferroni-corrected for retired families x sources (5 families: 2.61). (3) The pre-registered queue is reserved
  first: `research.reserved_trials_quarter: 13` (docs/research/preregistration-2027Q1.md) minus trials run against a
  `preregistered` registry row, at least the queued preregistered rows; the director and `monthly_research` spend
  only budget - used - reserved, and the plan's grid share is 0 while `research.label_grid_paused` (it is). With
  today's settings in Q1 2027: 20 - 13 = 7 planned trials, tsmom 6 and 1 shared by the five retired families. The
  plan records `evidence_budget`, `moves`, `quarter_reserved`, `reservation`, `retired_floor`, `retired_explore` and
  `reinstate_t`.

  runner (analyst, `research_pass.py`/`--discover` via `check_budget_reserved` -> `PreregisteredForLaterQuarter`, the
  label grid, which skips the variant) refuses a config queued for a later quarter (`director.later_preregistration`).
  An unlinked trial prefers the row of its own quarter. `preregister` has no `now=` (stamped by `registry._utcnow`), and
  `target_quarter` without `queue=True` is a ValueError. The digest adds "next quarter: N queued".
  For the owner / backlog (no code change): L2 research.reserved_trials_quarter (13) applies every quarter, so 2026Q4
  is also held to 7 open trials although its 13 queued trials are planned for 2027Q1 (owner decision: a per-quarter

- CUSUM re-verify fixes (M24/M25): h now sits halfway between the chosen reachable value of the statistic and the
  next higher one (`cusum.decision_interval`: same rate, but unrounded live sums can no longer turn a tie into an
  alarm); the drift watch calibrates on the agent's actual taken p values resampled per trade (`ps`), not their mean.
  Live false-alarm rates (production `residual_cusum` arithmetic, 200k paths, p spread per trade): 4.84-4.96% at p
  0.35-0.55 and 0.30-0.70 (the mean-p h gave 5.7-6.3% at 0.35-0.55; champion watch 2.6-2.9%). The new-champion watch runs two weeks or the
  first 12 trades, whichever is later, capped at 8 weeks, with h calibrated for that count (`cusum.watch_trades`);
  when the count cannot reach h it reports `cannot_alarm` (job output, `state/model_watch.json`, health warning
  `model_watch`) instead of a silent "ok": such slow agents rely on drift_watch and the drawdown halt.
- Approvals across processes (`telegram/bus.py`): engines, the API and the Telegram service are separate services,
  so engines publish proposals to `state/approvals/pending/`, the dashboard or Telegram writes a decision file
  (created exclusively: first decision wins), and the engine applies it on its next tick, re-running the RiskGate,
  then archives it in `approvals/done/` with the outcome. Owner halt: `state/control.json`, set by Telegram `/halt`
  or the dashboard (any approver); re-arm only on the dashboard by the owner with an authenticator code. Engines in
  production (`halt_checks`) also block entries when the supervisor's heartbeat is missing or stale. Exits are
  never gated.
- An approved order never exceeds its card (ADR 0009, 2026-10-11): the approval re-check can only reduce the size
  (`min(gate lots, card lots)`, journalled `approval_size_capped`), and a risk at the sent lots more than 2% above the
  card's `risk_amount` (the broker's conversion moved) is refused `risk_above_approved`. Proposals carry the
  account-currency risk, the minimum-lot note fields and the card's money (docs/ux/approval-card.md); restart
  engine, Telegram and API together with the engine last when deploying a proposal-format change (RUNBOOK).
- Clone mutations (`population.mutate_agent`): perturbed barriers/thresholds, a different feature subset
  (`feature_seed`: seeded 40 of the eligible features) or a different timeframe for breakout and mean_reversion
  (15m <-> 1h, holding horizon kept).
- Self-improvement loop (learns from past and present, changes only through gates): Saturday 03:17 UTC the data
  workflow appends the latest week of Dukascopy bars; 06:00 every population member is retrained on a rolling window
  ending at the latest bar, charged the canonical broker's measured slippage and commission from the nightly cost
  table (`jobs.live_extra_cost_usd`), and enters shadow as a challenger; it replaces the champion only when its live
  shadow record passes the promotion gates, and the daily CUSUM rolls a new champion back if live results drift.
  The tournament scores agents only on live shadow trades (expectancy, calibration of their own p, drawdown,
  correlation), clones winners into mutated children and retires losers; the research analyst tests hypotheses the
  improvement agent files from live scorecards. Every trial counts in the deflated Sharpe.
- One position per agent at a time (`labels.one_at_a_time`): research keeps a candidate only after the previous one
  exited, the shadow book refuses entries while the agent's trade is open, the engine skips an agent with an open
  position or pending proposal. Without it trend's clustered candidates overlapped and inflated every statistic.
- News blackout: `calendar_archive` (daily 06:10 UTC) stores the Forex Factory week in `calendar_events` with tiers
  (1 = US CPI/NFP/FOMC/PCE, 2 = other high-impact USD); production engines block entries from 15 min before to 30
  min after each tier-1 event, and for 30 min after a high-relevance unscheduled news shock. Headlines: service
  `goldbot-news` (`run.py news`) polls the RSS feeds in `settings.yaml: news` every 5 min, scores gold-relevant items
  in batches with structured output (budget `news.daily_cap_usd`, counted in the agents' monthly cap; unscored items
  are kept), stores them in `news`. The macro/news analyst writes the pre-session briefing (weekdays 06:30 UTC) from
  the calendar and headlines.
- Telegram service (`python -m goldbot.ops.run telegram`, NSSM `goldbot-telegram`): sends proposals with
  Approve/Reject buttons, posts each outcome, delivers every staff-agent report, answers /status and /halt
  (`telegram/outbox.py` keeps progress across restarts).
- One trial registry (`research/registry_sync.py`): the VPS monthly loop and the research workflow both union their
  registry with the `research-v1` release copy before and after writing, so the deflated Sharpe counts every trial once.
- Multi-timeframe: research, retrains, the dry run and the engine all build context with `features.mtf.context_tfs`
  (every one of 1h/4h/1d longer than the decision bar, prefixed h1_/h4_/d1_), so a model sees the columns it was
  trained on. The engine runs on its 15m clock and evaluates each agent only when a bar of the agent's own timeframe
  completes; context features are cached until a new context bar completes; open positions' time barriers and
  shadow trades count bars of the agent's timeframe.
- pandas 3 keeps s/ms/us timestamp units: always use `timeutil.epoch_ns`, never `.asi8`.
- Research discipline (proposal P1-P3, `docs/proposals/2026-10-design-improvements.md`): selection is cross-fitted
  (fold k calibrated only on earlier folds' OOF predictions; threshold from signal-time information); the cost hurdle
  is slippage + commission (`live_extra_cost_usd`, the settings prior before a cost table exists), not the spread
  again; `research/gates.py` checks 1,500 candidates / 60 per test fold / three positive years incl. 2021-22, and
  live promotion in the tournament needs a passed trial of the exact config; DSR is null below 200 trades; reports
  carry rule-only gross and net expectancy. Quarterly budget of 20 pre-registered trials
  (`research.trial_budget_quarter`), holdout 2025-10-01..2026-09-30 (`research_pass.py --score-holdout`, once per
  config), monthly label grid paused (`research.label_grid_paused`). Meta-models get `side` and side-aligned signed
  features (`features.registry.side_align`) from each specialist's declared `model_features` (h1_/h4_/d1_ context
  included). Fold-internal feature selection is deferred.
  Evaluator fixes (2026-10-08): research stops at the holdout start (no stub folds from later bars; the 60-per-fold
  gate counts complete folds only); gates include DSR >= 0.95 on 200+ model-filtered trades; `--score-holdout` needs a
  passed trial, is charged to the budget and is judged by its own rule (mean R > 0, t >= 1.65); one cap and one count
  for the quarterly budget (`registry.quarter_trials`, every row stamped in the quarter; the director plans from the
  same number); check-run-record under a portable registry lock; tournament, analyst trials and the paused monthly
  loop sync the release registry first; engine threshold and size multiplier use cost ex spread (RiskGate keeps the
  full round trip); signed-feature patterns are part of the feature version.
  Rule: a clone (new config hash) needs its OWN passed research trial before shadow -> live; nothing is inherited
  from its parent (the design counts real trials). Held-back agents show as `awaiting_research` in the tournament
  job's output.
  Deferred (L4): ~~a `preregistered` status written before a trial runs~~ (done 2026-10-10, discovery), an `eval_version` field on registry rows,
  bootstrap confidence intervals on expectancy, and a seeded no-signal test (100 seeds, DSR < 0.5 in >= 95).
- Primary-signal screen and new families (proposal P4, 2026-10-09): `research/screen.py` measures the rule alone
  (every candidate, one position at a time, mid prices) over the research window (holdout excluded) and passes it
  only with gross mean R > 0, t >= 2.0 and >= 1,000 events; net R is reported, not a criterion. `research_pass.py`
  screens every configuration first and fits no model for one that fails (registry status `screened`) unless
  `--skip-screen` (recorded as `screen_skipped`). **A screen is a trial**: it selects rules on data, so each screened
  configuration is one registry row, charged to the quarter's budget and counted by the deflated Sharpe whether it
  passes or not; when it passes, the walk-forward that follows is the same trial (one row). New families, both
  registered and founders in the population: `tsmom` (1h, 4h option; vol-scaled trailing return over 24/120/480 h,
  on a fixed 4-hour schedule, barriers 3.0/1.5 ATR, 48 bars) and `intraday_momentum` (15m; at mid-session on the
  London or New York local clock, DST by zoneinfo, enter in the direction of the move since the session open, exit at
  the session close, stop 2.0 / target 3.0 ATR). Their features (`tsmom`, `intraday_session`, family `momentum`) are
  versioned registry features and pass the lookahead check; adding them changes `feature_version` for every family
  (no champion exists, so nothing live is affected; retrains pick it up). Swap (2026-10-09, horizon study): net research
  labels pay overnight financing for every broker server-day rollover held through (`triple_barrier(swap=...)`, x3 on
  `costs.swap_triple_weekday`), from `costs.swap_long/short_usd_per_lot` (prior -60 / 0 USD per lot per night;
  replace with the broker cost table, `CostTable.swap_*`, which `live_swap` prefers when present); the gross screen
  carries no cost. tsmom also runs on `timeframe: "1d"` (feature-day bars, no context timeframe; daily defaults in
  `timeframe_defaults`: 20/60/120-day vol-scaled returns with 60-day vol, every settlement, 3.0/1.5 ATR, 10 bars;
  walk-forward `WINDOWS["1d"]` train 60 / test 12 / step 12 months expanding). Event count on data-v1 (counted only,
  outcomes not looked at): 454 events 2010-05..2025-09 (~29 a year, mean hold 6.9 bars, 8 swap nights), so the
  screen's 1,000-event floor cannot be met: one position at a time caps a 10-day daily rule at roughly
  trading days / (mean hold + 1), ~500 in 15.75 years. The per-fold gate fails too (12-month folds hold 23-38; the
  first fold starts 2018-05 because the 200-row training minimum takes ~7 years to fill). The 1d trial's verdict is the
  event floor; its gross R is still reported. tsmom 4h with swap: 2,289 events, 79% held overnight, 1.78 nights per
  trade. Every walk-forward report also shows the design's gates applied to the rule alone (`rule_only_gates`: every
  candidate net of all costs, same folds and trial count), labelled "rule-only (informational; promotion still
  requires the model path)"; `passed_gates` reads only the model path's `gates`. 4h is
  research-only: `saturday_retrain` skips timeframes without a settings walk-forward window.

  converted to USD per lot per night: points via tick value, base/margin/deposit money via price when the currency is

- Live data into learning (P9, 2026-10-09): the shadow book records EVERY candidate a champion/challenger scores
  with its p, raw score, the threshold at the time and `taken` (p > threshold); one position per agent applies over
  all candidates (as research thins before the model filter), and promotion stats, the CUSUM, re-arm and the
  population count taken trades only. Books written before this load unchanged (trades taken, no threshold) and are
  never calibration data. Weekly `recalibrate` job (Saturday 11:30, after the retrain, before the tournament) refits
  only the probability map of each champion/challenger on `ShadowBook.outcomes` of the last 182 days: a Platt layer
  on logit(p) with pseudo-outcomes equal to the validated p worth 200 trades (`research.recal_prior_trades`), no
  update below 50 outcomes, p at most 0.05 from the validated calibrator. Each run REPLACES the layer, refitted from
  the validated map (stacking layers on overlapping 182-day windows compounded: an independent review measured a
  -0.166 total move against a 0.05 cap after 8 weeks); rows without a raw score are not used; stored as a minor version (new checksummed artefact, same
  version/status, `recalibrations` row with before/after ECE; also `state/recalibration.jsonl`). It promotes and
  retires nothing. The ECE after is in-sample. Not done from P9: the monthly refit / drift-triggered refit, recency
  weighting and the replay trial; owner vetoes are not in the shadow book (it is the model's own decision).

  Linux) offers a new main commit that passed CI (backend + frontend check-runs) with [Deploy]/[Skip]
  (`goldbot/ops/deploy.py`); the tap writes `state/deploy/approved.json` for that exact commit; the root-owned
  `/usr/local/sbin/goldbot-deploy` (copy of `goldbot/ops/linux/goldbot-deploy.sh`, timer every minute) re-checks main,
  fast-forward and CI, waits while an approval is pending, restarts (supervisor first), verifies every enabled service

  report, health `deploy`). The MT5 box is updated by hand only. Hardened after the security review: root never writes
  or follows anything in a service-user-writable directory (symlink-to-root attack), approval file opened O_NOFOLLOW
  and owner-checked, any failure after checkout rolls back, stability = no systemd restart for 90 s plus a
  supervisor heartbeat written after the restart (engines write only on ticks), copy in state/ written as the service
  user, approval opened O_NONBLOCK, CI read from the latest GitHub Actions runs only, no CLI approve.
- Drift and health (M26/M27, 2026-10-10): every fitted model stores its training distribution per input
  (`feature_ref`); the daily `drift_watch` job (23:40) rebuilds the last 30 days of candidates as in training and
  computes PSI on the top-10 inputs by gain (0.1 warns, 0.25 sizes the agent to 50%), ECE/Brier on the trailing 100
  taken shadow trades (ECE > 0.08 sizes down), a residual CUSUM (halts the agent) and each agent's 30-day drawdown;
  two halted agents or a drawdown > 1.5x backtest halt the system. Output `state/drift.json`; halts are sticky per
  champion version until the owner runs `python -m goldbot.ops.run drift-review --clear "<note>"`. The engine reads
  it (missing = no restriction, unreadable = halt), the gate reason is `drift_system_halt`, health check `drift`.
  Entries only; exits unaffected. Models trained before this have no reference: PSI is skipped for them.
